holidays.name: National Coffee Ice Cream Day
holidays.description: This is a day for people who can't pick between a morning pick-me-up and dessert. Grab a scoop of coffee ice cream, or make an affogato by pouring hot espresso over vanilla. Either way, you get dessert and caffeine at once.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance. It was created to celebrate the pairing of coffee and ice cream, and its exact origin is unclear.
holidays.funFact: Coffee-flavored ice cream has been around for well over a century. The Italian affogato, which means 'drowned' in Italian, is a close cousin of it.

holidays.name: Fight Procrastination Day
holidays.description: This day asks you to do the thing you've been putting off. Answer that email, fold that laundry, or start that project. Since it's a day about doing things now, you can't save the celebrating for later.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It was created as a nudge to stop delaying tasks and start checking them off.
holidays.funFact: The word 'procrastinate' comes from the Latin 'pro' (forward) and 'crastinus' (of tomorrow). It literally means to push something off until tomorrow.

holidays.name: National Read a Book Day
holidays.description: You have an excuse to ignore your phone and open a book. Pick a novel, a comic, or that cookbook you've never finished. Fifteen minutes with a good story counts as celebrating.
holidays.origin: This is a modern, unofficial observance that grew out of the United States. It was created to encourage people to make time for reading.
holidays.funFact: Many readers keep a 'to be read' pile of unread books at home. Some people say owning more books than you can read is a joy in itself.
